issues.description: The --auto-hybrid-regex flag is documented but not marked as deprecated

issues.description: The tip mentions \d matches Unicode digits but the example shows [0-9] which may be confusing
issues.current_content:
# \d matches any digit [0-9]
rg "\d+"             # Matches numbers like "42", "123"

!!! tip "Prefer Predefined Classes"
    Use predefined classes like `\d` instead of `[0-9]` and `\w` instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_]` for better readability and Unicode support. For example, `\d` matches Unicode digits in all scripts, not just ASCII 0-9.
issues.should_be: Should clarify that \d behavior depends on context or regex engine settings
issues.fix_suggestion: Update the tip to clarify: 'In the default regex engine, \d is equivalent to [0-9] (ASCII only). For Unicode digit support across all scripts, use \p{N} instead. PCRE2 may have different Unicode handling.'
issues.source_reference: Rust regex documentation shows \d is ASCII-only by default unless Unicode mode is enabled
